title: The ford of the wild cattle is settled at Àth fhiadhaich
summary: A household settles a stony crossing in the south-eastern hills where wild cattle come down to drink, and rears the calves born on the near bank apart from the wild herd until, within three generations, that ford's cattle are spoken of the length of the coast as the best in the hills.

title: Households build about the old landing at Ceann àrsaidh
summary: People out of the Red Hill's country find an old river landing on the Abhainn fhionn, stones set for a boat's keel by hands none living can name, and build their houses about it, naming the place for what they found.

title: Inis mhòr's two facing rows are raised
summary: Households settle Inis mhòr on the Abhainn ghorm and build their houses in two rows facing each other across a single trodden way, so that a neighbour's fire may be borrowed without crossing open ground in the rain; it is the oldest street any teller remembers on Dia-thìr.

title: Catrìona takes the hill of Dùn ìseal
summary: Catrìona, of the king's blood and two hundred and forty-seven years old, takes Dùn ìseal formally as the twelfth to hold it of the Stone Kings' line, known already for a memory that can give any household's line back seven names without pausing to think.

title: Seumas Òg takes the Red Hill
summary: A young man of seven-and-twenty named Seumas takes up the holding of the Red Hill his own line has kept since the palisade first burned, the same season Catrìona takes Dùn ìseal; his name will be the last the Red Hill's own spoken roll carries.

title: The two rolls are spoken whole at the ford in one night
summary: Eòin gives the whole roll of the Stone Kings from Ailean Mòr to Catrìona's own name, and Ùna gives the whole roll of the Red Hill from Beathag Ruadh to Seumas Òg's, from dusk to the grey before morning; it is the first time either roll is heard whole, and those nearest the king see him smile when his own name is spoken.

title: The lot for the slab is drawn from every part of the hills
summary: Where the lot for the keeper of the slab was once drawn only from households near the crack, it comes in these years to be drawn from every part of the hills alike, and Tobar dhìreach becomes a place walked to for its own sake by households whose grandparents never heard the crack mentioned.

title: The keepers of the slab settle at nine
summary: The keepers settle at nine, one drawn by lot for each of nine districts of the hills that no household has ever marked on the ground but every household somehow knows the edge of; the nine meet at the slab only when one of their number dies.

title: The handful comes to be burned all at once by agreement
summary: Without any lot or law behind it, every household in reach of another comes to burn its measured handful of coloured coal on the same dark night, each watching for the first low flame on the nearest hill before lighting its own; the night comes to be called the night of the handful.

title: Cnoc na Claise's household refuses its handful
summary: The descendants of Torcall Tochlair, who stayed by the trench where his brother was crushed, will not burn the handful with the rest of the hills and give no single answer twice for it; Catrìona sends no one to compel them, and none at the slab asks her to.

title: The cord of Dùn ìseal grows to nine hundred knots
summary: Finding she can no longer carry the whole tally of households in her own head, Catrìona sets her people to counting them plainly on a knotted cord, a knot to a hearth, which grows through her years of holding to some nine hundred knots, the largest count made on Dia-thìr in the age; the king's own kin are never upon it.

title: A nameless hand recuts the column at Cnoc ghorm
summary: A hand from Catrìona's own hill goes out to the ancient column at Cnoc ghorm and recuts its worn grooves along their old lines before the rain can lose them; some who come after hold that a single stroke changed in the recutting, though none can agree which, or prove any changed at all.

title: The tally stones of Seann Dunn are set back in their old order
summary: A family digging a house-floor into an old midden at Seann Dunn strikes a row of upright stones each cut with a single stroke, knows them for the tally stones of the coast's old people, and sets them back as they lay rather than break them for the floor, building further along the midden's shoulder instead.

title: The south-eastern coast rows its dead to Eilean ìseal
summary: The custom grows along the south-eastern coast of rowing the newly dead out to Eilean ìseal rather than burying them on the mainland shore, whether learned from the old coast people's graves across the strait or come to of itself; the tellings let the question stand unsettled.

title: Eilean chrom stays unfished
summary: No household puts out a boat to fish the waters of Eilean chrom, where Gilleasbuig Beag was left with no boat to come back in; his fire was seen three nights running the first year and then no more, and the island stays empty and unfished.

title: The nine keepers ask Catrìona to declare their charge
summary: The nine keepers of the slab come up together at the ford and ask Catrìona, then in her seventy-sixth year of holding, to declare their charge over the slab, the lot and the handful before the whole gathering so that no king after her may reach for it as Calum Ciar once did; she names the eldest of them by his own line before he finishes bowing.

title: Catrìona answers the keepers: not this year, ask me again
summary: Catrìona gives the nine keepers neither refusal nor consent, telling them only, "Not this year," and then, before the eldest can press her further, "Ask me again"; the nine go back to their own fires by the slab to wait.

title: Eòin Beul-binn and Ùna Ruadh die within two years of each other
summary: Eòin, whose voice carried the whole roll of the Stone Kings across one night at the ford, dies in his eightieth year, and Ùna, who answered him roll for roll for the Red Hill, follows him within two years in her seventy-third; the telling of that single night passes from then on at second hand.

title: Catrìona falls ill on the hill
summary: In her two hundred and eighty-ninth year the sickness comes on Catrìona that will not leave again; she keeps her seat at Dùn ìseal as long as she is able, still able to give a household's whole line back seven names, and the nine keepers, hearing of it, send no word asking again.
